Question
========
Which of the following statements about the syntax of strings in JSON are correct?

Answerlist
----------
* A string can be wrapped in either single or double quotation marks, whichever the author prefers.
* Certain characters, such as the quotation mark itself or the backslash, must be escaped using a reverse solidus (backslash).
* A Unicode code point can be represented using a hexadecimal escape sequence, such as `\u0041`.
* A JSON string is only allowed to contain plain ASCII characters, so accented letters like "ü" can never appear directly in a string.


Solution
========
A JSON string always has to be wrapped in double quotation marks - single quotes are not valid JSON, unlike in some other languages. Certain characters, including the double quote and the backslash itself, need to be escaped with a reverse solidus so they are not mistaken for part of the syntax. Any Unicode code point can also be written out as a hexadecimal escape sequence, for example `\u0041` for the letter "A". Beyond that, JSON strings are not limited to ASCII at all - since JSON text is Unicode by nature, characters like "ü" or "ö" can be written directly in a string without any escaping.

Answerlist
----------
* False
* True
* True
* False
